description: Three effects in a row — a stereo delay, a granular section and a reverb — each with its own dry-wet control and its own switch to let a chaotic signal generated inside the module drift its settings

params.text: Sets the delay on the left side, 1ms to 2 seconds
Sets the delay on the right side, 1ms to 2 seconds
Sets how much of the delayed signal is written back into the line, 0% to 95%
Lets the chaotic signal drift the two delay times and the feedback; the lamp on it is lit while it is on
Crossfades the delay against the signal coming in, 0% for the dry signal alone and 100% for the delay alone; whatever comes out of here is what the granular section is given
Sets how fast the chaotic signal moves: a hundredth of its base speed to its base speed with SHAPE off, and one to ten times it with SHAPE on
Sets the length of each grain, 1ms at the bottom of its travel to 100ms at the top
Sets how often a new grain is started, one per second at the bottom of its travel to fifty-one per second at the top, and also sets the pre-delay of the reverb
Sets how far back in the recorded buffer the grains are read from
Lets the chaotic signal scatter the grain positions and rate, with the right side taking the opposite sign from the left; the lamp on it is lit while it is on
Crossfades the granular section against what the delay stage handed it, 0% for that signal alone and 100% for the grains alone; whatever comes out of here is what the reverb is given
Sets the size of the reverb space, lengthening the comb delays and the extra taps as it is turned up
Sets how much of the high end the reverb loses on each pass, a little at the bottom of its travel and most of it at the top
Sets how long the reverb tail rings on, and with it how much of the reverb is fed back into the delay line
Lets the chaotic signal shift the reverb's comb delay taps; the lamp on it is lit while it is on
Crossfades the reverb against what the granular stage handed it, 0% for that signal alone and 100% for the reverb alone
Scales the chaotic signal before anything uses it, 0 to 1; at zero nothing drifts and the CV output rests at 0V
Switches the chaotic signal between a smooth drift and a stepped one that holds each value until the next sample is taken; the lamp beside it is lit while it is stepped

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to be treated; with nothing patched to the right jack this one feeds both sides
The right side of the signal to be treated
Added to the TIME L knob, a fifth of a second per volt; the total is held between 1ms and 2 seconds
Added to the TIME R knob, a fifth of a second per volt; the total is held between 1ms and 2 seconds
Added to the FDBK knob, ten points of feedback per volt; the total is held between 0% and 95%
Added to the SIZE knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the BREAK knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the SHIFT knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the ROOM knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the TONE knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the reverb DECAY knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it

outputs.text: The left side of the chain, delay into grains into reverb
The right side of the chain, delay into grains into reverb
The chaotic signal itself, ±5V, scaled by the AMOUNT knob and stepped or smooth according to SHAPE

notes: all three effects start with their dry-wet controls at 0%, so the module passes the signal through untouched until one of those three knobs is turned up.
the reverb is fed back into the delay line in proportion to the reverb DECAY setting, so a long tail and high feedback together can run away.
the BREAK knob does double duty: it sets the grain rate and it also sets the reverb's pre-delay.
